summary: The Russian Government quota gives foreign citizens a place to study at a Russian university, financed from the federal budget. It is run by the Russian Ministry of Science and Higher Education with Rossotrudnichestvo, which holds the first selection stage in the candidate's home country, and applications go through the official portal for foreign citizens. About 15,000 foreign candidates a year are offered state-funded study, at levels from bachelor's to postgraduate and residency, and applicants who do not know Russian can start with a preparatory year. The official pages state tuition as the free element; stipend and other costs are not stated.
eligibility_notes:
Only foreign citizens may apply. A person who also holds Russian citizenship may apply only if they live permanently abroad and have no education document issued in the Russian format.

The applicant needs at least secondary general or secondary vocational education to enter a Russian university. Russian law sets no age limit for applicants. A student who already studies in Russia at their own expense can compete for the quota on general terms when moving to the next level; selection then takes place in their country of citizenship.

The number of quota places per country depends on intergovernmental agreements and is tied to fields of study that match the country's need for specialists (for example engineers for a joint nuclear power project); the portal's online monitoring section shows the places for the year.

Knowledge of Russian is not a mandatory requirement. It counts as an advantage in selection, and many universities offer programmes taught in English. A candidate who does not speak Russian can tick the preparatory-year option in the application and will be sent to a Russian-language course before the main programme.

The first stage is run in the candidate's own country by a Rossotrudnichestvo office (Russian House) or Russian consular body, and details, dates and status questions depend on the country; candidates are told to contact the office or embassy for their country.
age_experience_notes: No age limit and no work experience requirement are stated. The FAQ says Russian law does not limit the age of applicants.
funding_summary: The official pages describe the quota as financing of tuition from the federal budget; the FAQ says that in all free-study routes only tuition is free and the student needs money for travel, health insurance, housing and everyday costs. A preparatory year in Russian is available to applicants who need it. The pages read do not state a monthly stipend, a travel grant, how long funding lasts for each level, or any housing or insurance payment.
programmes_note: Levels offered through the portal are bachelor's, master's, specialist, postgraduate (aspirantura), adjunct, residency (ordinatura) and assistantship-internship programmes, in full-time, part-time or distance form. The applicant chooses the level, the specialty and the form of study in the application. Study is in any field offered by the chosen universities and in the places allocated for the candidate's country. For residency and postgraduate applicants a motivation letter and an abstract or article about the planned research are also required.
institutions_note: The portal says 741 universities from 82 regions of Russia take part. In the application the candidate lists up to six universities in order of preference, with no more than two in Moscow, no more than two in Saint Petersburg and no more than three in one federal district. Candidates who pass the first stage are distributed to universities by the ministry; a quota student cannot simply change university, and transfers or changes of specialty, including after the preparatory year, are for the Ministry of Science and Higher Education to decide.

summary.detail: Bachelor's (and specialist) programmes are open under the quota. Applicants from CIS countries, Ukraine and South Ossetia sat online proctored subject tests in April 2026 (chemistry, biology, physics, mathematics, Russian language, history, depending on the chosen direction). Duration of study and teaching language are not stated by the pages; applicants without Russian can take a preparatory year first.

Master's programmes are open under the quota in any field of the participating universities. Duration, teaching language and subject list are not stated; the FAQ notes many universities teach some programmes in English.

Postgraduate studies (aspirantura) and adjunct programmes are open under the quota; residency (ordinatura) and assistantship-internship are also listed. Applicants for postgraduate and residency places must add a motivation letter and an abstract or article on the planned research. Duration is not stated.

benefits.limit_text: Tuition-free study at a Russian university, financed from the federal budget
benefits.conditions: Applies to quota places only. Students sent by the ministry to a university by allocation; no change of university without the ministry's decision.

benefits.limit_text: Preparatory year in Russian for applicants who need it, if requested in the application form
benefits.conditions: Usually one year, normally October to June; at the end the student takes a Russian language exam and, if passed, is placed on the main programme by allocation. The pages do not say whether the preparatory year is paid separately.

benefits.limit_text: No monthly stipend amount is stated on the official pages read
benefits.conditions: The FAQ only notes that students who receive a stipend must open an account with a Russian bank.

benefits.limit_text: Dormitory places are offered by universities where space exists, for a rent; the FAQ gives 500 to 5,000 roubles per month, another portal page gives 300 to 20,000 roubles per month (about 3.7 to 225 euros)
benefits.conditions: Rent depends on the university and city. Private renting is the alternative. The pages do not say the quota pays for housing.

benefits.limit_text: Voluntary medical insurance is bought by the student: the FAQ says about 6,000 to 9,000 roubles a year, another portal page says about 4,000 to 20,000 roubles (45 to 255 euros); minimum insured sum 100,000 roubles
benefits.conditions: Required for every foreign student on arrival; living without a policy can lead to a fine.

benefits.limit_text: Travel to Russia is not named as covered
benefits.conditions: The FAQ says the free element is only tuition and students need funds to reach the university.

requirements.text: Scan of the passport (or other identity document)
Scan of the education document; applicants still studying upload a certificate from their place of study
Scan of the transcript or grade sheet
Application questionnaire and consent to personal data processing, scanned (named in the notice for Syrian citizens; the general notice lists an application form and photograph in the process page)
requirements.conditional_rule: Named explicitly for Syrian citizens; the portal's general process also lists a completed questionnaire and a photograph

requirements.text: Abstract or article on the topic of the planned research
All documents translated into Russian and certified by a notary or consul; the university may ask for more documents after admission

Documents handed to the university admissions office on arrival: application for admission; identity and citizenship document with notarised translation; education document showing qualification, subjects and grades with notarised translation; medical certificate of no HIV infection and no contraindications to study, in Russian or with notarised translation; photograph. Check whether the documents need legalisation in the country of issue, or an apostille if the country joined the Hague Convention.

application_steps.title: Choose level, specialty and universities
application_steps.detail: Decide the level of study, the form of study and the field, and look through the participating universities (741 in 82 regions). Quota candidates are advised to contact a Rossotrudnichestvo office or consulate in their country, which runs the competition there. Place up to six universities in order of preference, at most two in Moscow, two in Saint Petersburg and three in one federal district.

application_steps.title: Register on the portal and create a new application
application_steps.detail: Register on the official portal for foreign citizens, open the My applications section and create a new application. Choose the level, specialty and universities, say whether a preparatory course is needed, and upload scans of the passport, education document (or study certificate) and transcript. Residency and postgraduate applicants add the motivation letter and research abstract or article.

application_steps.title: Send the application for review before the closing date
application_steps.detail: Press the button that sends the application for review; applications left in draft status do not enter the competition. For 2026/27 applications opened on 15 September 2025 and closed on 15 January 2026 for most candidates; nine countries had later dates, for example Georgia 15 February, Vietnam 31 March, Botswana 15 March, Serbia 31 January. The hotline of Rossotrudnichestvo for quota questions is +7 985 870-21-27.

application_steps.title: First stage in your country: interview and selection tests
application_steps.detail: Depending on the country, candidates may have an interview with Rossotrudnichestvo or a Russian consular body and take selection exams. Register for the event in your personal account and take part in the form set. The points decide your rank among candidates from your country. In 2026 bachelor and specialist applicants from CIS countries, Ukraine and South Ossetia sat online proctored tests on 20 to 30 April; reserve days were held for chemistry, biology, physics, mathematics, Russian and history.

application_steps.title: Second stage: universities review applications
application_steps.detail: Candidates who pass the first stage move to the second stage, where universities consider the applications. Some universities set extra entrance tests, online or in person; in-person tests need a visa if required and travel to Russia on set dates. The result in the personal account names the university where you will study.

application_steps.title: Receive the study referral and prepare documents
application_steps.detail: The result and arrival details appear in the personal account; agree the arrival date with the university. Prepare the admission documents with certified translations and, if needed, legalisation or apostille. Applicants who need Russian are told which university gives the preparatory course.

application_steps.title: Get the study visa and travel to Russia
application_steps.detail: A passport and study visa are needed unless the country has visa-free entry with Russia. For quota students Rossotrudnichestvo handles the invitation: the ministry's visa instruction is sent to the Russian embassy and its number, date and validity appear in the personal account. The portal does not send invitations itself.

application_steps.title: Insure, register and start studying
application_steps.detail: On arrival buy voluntary medical insurance and hand the documents to the university admissions office. The academic year runs from 1 September to 30 June; preparatory courses usually start in October. Students who took a preparatory year sit a Russian exam at the end and are then placed on the main programme by allocation.

not_stated: Monthly stipend amount, travel grant or housing allowance for quota students
How long funding lasts at each level (duration of bachelor's, master's and postgraduate study)
Minimum language level or language test score (Russian is stated as not mandatory)
Minimum grades or exam scores needed to pass the first stage
Number of quota places for each country (the portal's online monitoring shows them)
A list of programmes per level: the portal has a searchable catalogue only

fetch_problems: education-in-russia.com is a JavaScript application; the page-reading tool returned only the title, so the same official pages were read through the site's own public content feed (the page text is identical to what the site shows).
The English instruction PDF on the portal returned HTTP 502 on three attempts.
Rossotrudnichestvo and Russian House in Dhaka pages (rs.gov.ru) showed a browser check and were not bypassed; the Ministry of Science and Higher Education site redirected to a maintenance page.
The portal's admission-process page text is in Russian in the content feed and was translated and paraphrased.
notes: Contradiction on the portal: the process page says in one paragraph to list 'at least six' universities and in another 'not more than six'; the notice of 15 September 2025 says up to six. This file says up to six.

Stored statement 'per the Russian House in Dhaka, students are responsible only for accommodation and health insurance' is carried over from stored data; it was not re-confirmed because that site is behind a browser check. The portal FAQ says the free element is tuition only and students also pay for travel, insurance, housing and daily costs.

Stored milestone 'application period Bangladesh route 15 September 2025 to 15 January 2026' matches the general dates on the portal notices; the reserve-day history test on 28 April 2026 matches the portal's schedule and results notices.
Dormitory and insurance cost figures differ between pages of the same portal (see benefits); both ranges are given.
The Open Doors scholarship project is a separate programme and is not covered here.
